name: Caspofungin
executiveSummary: Echinocandin. Adult: load **70 mg** day 1, then **50 mg/day** (70 mg/day if > 80 kg or severe). Pediatrics > 3 months: load **70 mg/m²**, then **50 mg/m²/day** (max 70 mg).
indications:
## Indications

- Invasive candidiasis, candidemia, candida esophagitis.
- Invasive aspergillosis refractory/intolerant to other azoles/amphotericin.
- Empiric therapy in febrile neutropenia.

## Precautions

- Adjust in moderate hepatic impairment (adult maintenance **35 mg/day**).
- Interactions: inducers (rifampin, etc.) may require **70 mg/day** maintenance.
- Do not dilute in dextrose on many labels — use **NS**.

> No PO. Infuse ~1 h.

adulto.dose: Load: **70 mg IV** day 1. Maintenance: **50 mg/day**. If weight > 80 kg or aspergillosis/severe: maintenance **70 mg/day**. Child-Pugh B hepatic: maintenance **35 mg/day** after 70 mg load.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute with sterile water; dilute in **250 mL NS**; infuse ~**60 min**. No bolus. Do not mix with dextrose on many brands.
adulto.notes: Switch to another echinocandin/azole by course and culture.

pediatrico.dose: > 3 months: load **70 mg/m²** (max **70 mg**), then **50 mg/m²/day** (max **70 mg**). If inducers or poor response: up to **70 mg/m²/day** (max 70 mg). Neonates: **2 mg/kg/day** only with ID authorization.

neonatal.dose: Orientative off-label: **2 mg/kg/day** under ID — not routine.
neonatal.notes: Limited data; prefer validated NNU schemes.

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution in NS: per label (usually 24 h refrigerated).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Fever, phlebitis, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, ↑ transaminases, rash, hypokalemia, anemia.
